newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Pioneer says no decision on Ampol yet.
newsitem.headline: Pioneer says no decision on Ampol yet.

text.p: Pioneer International Ltd said on Thursday it has not yet made a decision about its 50 percent stake in Australia's largest petroleum refiner and marketer, Ampol, which has suffered a sharp fall in profitability.
"We are still evaluating our options, but it is progressing," Pioneer chief executive officer John Schubert told reporters after giving a speech to an Australia-Israel Chamber of Commerce luncheon.
Schubert said the company was talking to a number of parties about a possible sale.
Pioneer started a review of its Ampol investment began in January due to an unsatisfactory return on shareholders funds.
He said Pioneer would only sell its Ampol stake if it added shareholder value and the funds from the sale would be invested into its core business of concrete, cement and quarrying.

Schubert said local regulation was putting pressure on refiner margins. "There are some aspects of regulation that puts refiner marketers at a disadvantage to the independents or to the importers and it doesn't really make sense," Schubert said.
Ampol is the trading name of Australia Petroleum Pty Ltd, which Pioneer jointly owns with Caltex Australia Ltd.
At 3.15 p.m. (0505 GMT), Pioneer shares were five cents lower at A$4.39.
